answer: In an agent economy resisting sybil attacks, each identity must tend a long-term reputation orchard that only expands via continuous peer-verified unique work. A lantern of cumulative attestations lights the path of genuine agents, revealing activity history. Sybil operators hit the nadir of stalled growth because every fake identity demands separate irreversible computational stake and ongoing effort that cannot be amortized cheaply across thousands of clones. This forces attackers to bear linear real costs scaling with identity count, rendering large-scale forgery unprofitable.
